summary.headline: Solex Q1 FY27 revenue rose 1.8% YoY to INR265.6 crore while PAT fell to INR8.3 crore (3.1% margin) on higher depreciation and finance costs.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR265.6 crore, up 1.8% YoY from INR261 crore, but EBITDA fell to INR33.8 crore (12.7% margin vs 16.4%). Depreciation rose to INR10.2 crore and finance cost to INR12.5 crore, taking PAT to INR8.3 crore (3.1% margin). Management attributed the weak quarter to seasonality, ALMM-2 (ALCM) timing shifts that delayed module off-take, and full-quarter costs of the 4 GW capacity, and reiterated FY27 guidance of a 5-6% PAT margin with an H2-weighted year. Management also flagged progress on a 2.2 GW cell line, with funding and land still pending.

segments.name: Module manufacturing (4 GW, Tadkeshwar, Gujarat)
segments.commentary: Four module lines operating; lines 3 and 4 commissioned November 2025 and reached full utilisation by March 2026. FY27 average utilisation assumed at about 55%, versus about 70% in FY26 per an analyst question.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Not a focus; management targets INR100-150 crore of EPC business at a 10-12% margin, mainly C&I projects of 1-5 MW and rooftop. Government EPC revenue booked in Q1 FY26 was not repeated.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance and PAT margin of 5-6% reiterated.
FY27 module utilisation assumed at about 55% on average across the year.
Executable order pipeline of INR845.84 crore (INR628+ crore order from July, INR42.47 crore order from August, INR175 crore LOI with MSA at signing stage) targeted for execution by December 31, 2026.
2.2 GW N-type TOPCon+ cell line on track for commissioning by end of calendar 2027.
Vision 2030: 10 GW module, 10 GW cell, 10 GW BESS and 2 GW wafer/ingot capacity; INR4,000 crore MoU with Government of Gujarat.
Module capex reduced: planned 2.5 GW module line dropped; cell project cost now about INR1,050 crore (INR700 crore debt, INR350 crore equity via NCDs/CCDs).
capex_capacity: Module capacity 4 GW at Tadkeshwar, Gujarat; lines 3 and 4 commissioned November 2025.
2.2 GW cell line (phase 1 of 5 GW single-site cell plan; phase 2 of 3 GW). Commissioning targeted by end CY2027.

Cell project cost about INR1,050 crore: debt of about INR700 crore at advanced discussion with lender; equity of INR350 crore via NCDs/CCDs in due diligence. QIP/preferential route abandoned due to market conditions.
Land: parcel procured per management; 30 MW power connection in Gujarat has verbal approval, written approval awaited.
Cell technology partner and KPI-linked operator being onboarded for line design, commissioning and operations.
BESS: containerised manufacturing setup under evaluation with technology partners; to sit in a separate subsidiary. No timeline given beyond 'coming quarters'.
demand_pricing: Order book approximately INR3,400 crore (per management), across confirmed POs, signed MSAs awaiting POs, and advanced-stage MSAs; management says visibility is not contingent on ALMM-2 outcome.
ALMM-2 (ALCM) on cells: no extension announced on 25 May 2026, causing project holds and customer-driven delivery rescheduling in Q1 and Q2. Management calls these timing shifts, not cancellations.
Management estimated about 20% of orders have vulnerability from the captive/DCR segment; said this was resolved by the government's selective extension to December 2026 for commissioning.

Domestic DCR cell supply constrained: three Indian cell makers supply small volumes; one partner to supply 1 GW per year after ramp-up; total about 2.5 GW per year of G12R cells expected from MoU partners.
Export focus: Europe, Middle East, Africa, with US market being tested; FY27 export revenue projected to be low.
OEM/contract manufacturing for global brands under discussion; two global top-five brands already served; Q4 FY27 targeted for Indian projects.
Customer concentration: largest closed order above INR600 crore; second INR175 crore; third INR42 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the capex plan change from INR1,500 crore (INR1,100 crore cell, INR200 crore module, INR100 crore working capital) to INR1,050 crore cell project funded INR700 crore debt and INR350 crore equity, and which figure should be used for FY27 modelling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the earlier plan included an additional 2.5 GW module line, which has been dropped given market conditions, reducing roughly INR200 crore. The current cell project cost is about INR1,050 crore for the 2.2 GW line: INR700 crore from principal lenders and INR350 crore as promoter margin.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory rose from INR1,795 million to INR2,905 million in FY26; is there obsolescence or write-down risk from technology change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the inventory build seasonal, with the same H1 pattern in FY26 and in the current period, and said the company makes the latest G12R generation, so no technology obsolescence impact. Inventory is expected to clear after monsoon; H2 vs H1 gap cited as roughly 1:3.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 weak when historically Q1 is not this weak, and monsoon was delayed so execution should have been stronger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to lines 3 and 4 running with full interest and depreciation against lower revenue, and to absence of Q1 FY26 government EPC revenue. It attributed module delays to the ALMM-2 clarity gap, with the 1 June deadline and about 9,500 extension applications, and said orders are deferred, not cancelled.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the order book is exposed to ALMM-2, and what cell supply arrangements exist for DCR orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most grandfathered projects are unaffected and about 20% of orders have vulnerability from the captive/DCR segment, now addressed by the extension to December 2026. Three Indian cell makers supply small volumes; one partner will supply 1 GW per year after ramp-up; about 2.5 GW per year of G12R cells is expected from MoU partners, mainly from next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the largest customer concentration and the EPC order book and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Largest closed order is above INR600 crore, second is INR175 crore (LOI, MSA at signing), third is INR42 crore from a domestic captive project. EPC is not a focus; target is INR100-150 crore at a 10-12% margin, mainly C&I projects of 1-5 MW and rooftop.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 module utilisation assumed at 55% versus about 70% in FY26 despite the larger 4 GW base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited an industry average utilisation of about 50%, the ALMM-related disruption, and the domestic cell shortage, calling the 55% assumption conservative. Capacity rose from 1.5 GW to 4 GW.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cell line status on land, power, and funding, and how does execution risk compare with peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Land parcel is procured per management; a 30 MW Gujarat power connection has verbal approval with written approval awaited. Debt of about INR700 crore is at advanced discussion; the INR350 crore equity via NCDs/CCDs is in due diligence; QIP/preferential route was dropped. The company said a TOPCon operator will be onboarded on a KPI-linked basis and that the 5 GW single site is being built in two phases.

risks_watch: ALMM-2 (cell) policy: no extension announced on 25 May 2026; captive/DCR orders depend on the December 2026 commissioning extension, and about 20% of orders are flagged as vulnerable.

Domestic DCR cell supply: only small volumes today, 1 GW per year from one partner after ramp-up, and about 2.5 GW per year of G12R cells expected from MoU partners, which are converting lines from G12 to G12R. Timing is uncertain.

Cell project funding and approvals: INR700 crore debt at advanced discussion, INR350 crore equity via NCDs/CCDs still in due diligence, and the 30 MW Gujarat power connection awaiting written approval. Commissioning is targeted for end-CY2027.
Working capital and finance cost: finance cost rose to INR12.5 crore from INR5.4 crore, with more reliance on fund-based limits. Inventory rose to INR2,905 million in FY26 from INR1,795 million.

Guidance credibility: FY27 PAT margin guidance of 5-6% against a Q1 PAT margin of 3.1%, with a 55% utilisation assumption and an H2-weighted year. Q2 is already seen following the same seasonal pattern.

Order book quality: the INR3,400 crore book mixes confirmed POs, signed MSAs awaiting POs and advanced MSAs; only the INR845.84 crore executable pipeline is targeted for execution by December 31, 2026. Track PO conversion next quarter.
Export and OEM diversification: FY27 export revenue is projected to be low. OEM work for global brands for Indian projects is targeted for Q4 FY27.
key_quotes: These are the timing shifts and not cancellations.
Investors should see Q1 as a near-term operating cycle and cell manufacturing as a medium-term earnings inflection.
We remain aligned with the FY27 revenue guidance and PAT margin in the range of 5% to 6%.
We will announce everything once the finance closure is done and then we get a confirmation from the electricity connection.
summary.management_tone: Management is confident on the H2 recovery and the order book, but cautious and sometimes evasive on near-term numbers. It is firm that Q1 is seasonal and that ALMM-2 effects are timing rather than cancellations. It is less specific on cell-project funding and land timelines, and on BESS, where it gave no timeline.
